question: Can an ad be misleading under Canadian competition law even if its individual words are technically true?

Backgrounder

The Competition Bureau has filed an application with the Competition Tribunal, alleging that Volkswagen Canada Inc. (“VW”) has made false or misleading representations to the public in its advertising for certain 2017 and 2018 model year vehicles. The Competition Tribunal will hear the case at a future date. The Competition Act prohibits the making of false or misleading representations to the public for the purpose of promoting products or services. VW has promoted its TDI Clean Diesel technology as a “clean diesel” that is environmentally friendly, and has also claimed that TDI Clean Diesel technology meets and exceeds the environmental standards of the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). According to the Competition Bureau’s application, these claims are false or misleading because VW’s TDI Clean Diesel technology does not actually meet or exceed the environmental standards of the EPA. The Competition Bureau alleges that VW’s TDI Clean Diesel technology does not meet the EPA standards for nitrogen oxide emissions. The Competition Bureau also alleges that VW has made false or misleading representations in its advertising in that it has failed to disclose the presence of a device called a “defeat device” in its TDI Clean Diesel technology. A defeat device is a device that is designed to produce lower emissions of nitrogen oxides when the vehicle is being tested than during normal operation. VW has admitted that defeat devices were installed in its TDI Clean Diesel technology. The Competition Bureau’s application also alleges that VW has made false or misleading representations in its advertising by claiming that its TDI Clean Diesel technology is “clean diesel” technology that is environmentally friendly. The Competition Bureau alleges that these claims are false or misleading because VW’s TDI Clean Diesel technology does not actually meet or exceed the environmental standards of the EPA. The Competition Bureau seeks an order from the Competition Tribunal requiring VW to cease making false or misleading representations in its advertising, and to pay an administrative monetary penalty of up to $10 million. The Competition Tribunal will hear the case at a future date. The Competition Act does not provide for monetary remedies for individual consumers.
